prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Code · Config options with long tokens (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Option" · longest unbreakable word 131px · one-line width 131px
  col 2: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 90px · one-line width 334px
  col 3: header "Example" · longest unbreakable word 537px · one-line width 537px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 501px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A configuration reference table: readers scan option names, compare defaults with concrete examples, and consult descriptions for meaning.","reading":"Row-by-row lookup, with Option as the anchor; Default and Example are compared as parallel values, while Description is supporting prose read only when needed.","groups":["Option + Description: name and meaning for each row","Default + Example: parallel value columns with the same comparison role"],"keep_intact":["Option identifiers such as auth.jwksUri","Example URLs and log-format strings where possible","Default format-string tokens such as %d{ISO8601} %-5level %logger{36}"],"may_wrap":["Description prose","Default values at spaces between tokens","Example URLs only when accepting word splitting in a no-scroll design"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[152,200,558,240],"idea":"Horizontal-scroll layout that keeps Option and the 537px Example token intact while Default and Description wrap naturally."},{"name":"B","widths":[152,165,250,152],"idea":"No-scroll balanced layout: preserve Option exactly, give Example the largest remaining share, and let Default and Description wrap; URLs split."},{"name":"C","widths":[152,140,300,127],"idea":"No-scroll Example-first layout: widen Example to reduce URL fragmentation, at the cost of tighter Default and Description columns."}]}
